name: common-qa-mcp

tools.name: project_info
tools.description: Validate the configured connection and return provider, org/project and entity counts.

tools.name: qa_connect
tools.description:
Point this MCP at your QA product so it can work with EXISTING test cases -- list them, read their steps, modify them, and run them. Ask the user for their app URL and a token; do not guess either. The token is a product session JWT (then `projectId` is required, because the token alone carries no project context) or an MCP API key (then pass auth:"key" and projectId is optional -- a key is already project-scoped).

The connection is VALIDATED before it is accepted (it fetches the project), so a wrong URL, token or project fails here with the reason rather than surfacing later as a confusing error, and a failed attempt leaves any working connection untouched. It is kept in memory for as long as the agent runs and is never written to disk or logged.

NOT needed to record a new test case: recording, the live editor and drafts work offline with nothing configured.

url.description: MCP endpoint to hop to — the product agent /mcp, used for recording and save-with-editor. OPTIONAL for a DIRECT (backend-REST) connection: pass `baseUrl` instead. Required when connecting through a remote product MCP. Must start with http:// or https://.

token.description: Bearer token: a product session JWT, or an MCP API key.

projectId.description: Project id. REQUIRED with a JWT; optional with an API key.

auth.description: Token kind. Omit to AUTO-DETECT from the token (JWT-shaped → "jwt"). "jwt" sends Authorization + x-project-id; "key" sends Authorization only.

product.description: Which product to route this connection to (the product selector; defaults to the primary product). For a remote product, also pass its agent MCP `/mcp` endpoint as `url`.

baseUrl.description: The product BACKEND REST base (QA_BASE_URL) for DIRECT data ops (list/read/save/run). Provide this for a direct connection; `url` is only needed for recording / save-with-editor.

tools.name: qa_switch_project
tools.description: Switch to a different project on the SAME connection — reuses the current URL + token, so you do NOT re-enter them. Pass the project id; if the user names a project, call list_projects first to resolve the name to an id. Validated before it is adopted, so a bad id leaves the current project in place.

projectId.description: The project id to switch to. Use list_projects to find it by name.

tools.name: qa_connection_status
tools.description: Report whether this MCP is connected to a QA product, which URL and project, how the credentials arrived (startup config vs qa_connect), and whether a token is present. The token value itself is never returned.

tools.name: qa_disconnect
tools.description: Forget the runtime URL and token and fall back to whatever the agent started with (usually nothing). Use it before connecting to a different app or project, or to stop this MCP reaching a backend at all. Offline authoring is unaffected.

tools.name: actions_catalog
tools.description: Static per-platform action-type vocabulary (web/android/api/database/mainframe), used for offline draft validation. No network call.

tools.name: tc_draft_create
tools.description:
Create a new in-memory test-case draft from steps you author yourself. Nothing is persisted -- no disk, no backend, no network. Use tc_draft_open to hand it to the test-case editor for viewing.

DO NOT USE THIS FOR A REAL WEB APPLICATION. Steps written here have no locators, so the test case cannot execute -- it only reads plausibly. Whenever there is an app you can reach (the user gives a URL, names an environment, or asks for a test of a real flow), call `recording_start` instead and drive the app with `browser_*`: that captures real locators, real element names and real parameters, and is the DEFAULT way to create a web test case. You do not need the user to say "record" -- if a test case for a real app is wanted, recording is how it is made.

Legitimate uses: a manual test case (no automation), API/database steps that need no element binding, restructuring or drafting steps the user supplied verbatim, or sketching a plan when no app is reachable -- and say plainly that the result is not executable until recorded.

INPUT VALUES MUST BE PARAMETERIZED. When a step has a value (text to type, a URL to open, an expected string), put a `${param}` token in its description AND set the step `value` -- e.g. description "Enter ${username} in the Username field", value "standard_user". On save these bind into the test case's default test-data row (the dataset the product auto-creates), so it can run with data. A value with no `${param}` in the same description has nowhere to bind and is dropped -- this is how the product stores web values (never inline on the step).

storyRef.description: Link this test case to a USER STORY — its id or business key (US_123, from story_list / story_get). Used when drafting MANUAL test cases for a story so they save linked to it.

folderOrModule.description: SimplifyQA-only: id of the MODULE / folder to file this test case under on save (from list_modules). ASK the user which module before drafting; SimplifyQA files test cases in a module tree. Walnut ignores this.

tools.name: tc_draft_update
tools.description: Apply one or more ops (set_meta | add_step | update_step | remove_step | move_step) to a draft. Steps renumber contiguously from 1 after every op.

tools.name: tc_draft_get
tools.description: Fetch a draft by id: readable steps table, validation summary, and the neutral TestCase.

tools.name: tc_draft_discard
tools.description: Delete an in-memory draft. Nothing was ever persisted, so there is nothing else to undo.

tools.name: tc_draft_open
tools.description: Show this draft in the product's real editor. Prefers the local agent's own native window when the agent is running; otherwise returns a link to open. The draft rides in the URL fragment -- nothing is uploaded, no backend call is made.

tools.name: tc_save
tools.description:
Validate a draft, then PERSIST it to the connected product — creating a NEW test case, or UPDATING the one it was opened from (when the draft carries an id). Returns the product id + a deep link. Requires a live connection (qa_connect); the persist is forwarded to the product MCP.
⚠️ CALL ONLY ON AN EXPLICIT USER SAVE INSTRUCTION (e.g. "save it", "save this", "persist it"). RECORDING or AUTHORING a test case is NOT a save instruction; neither is the user approving the content ("looks good", "nice"). After a recording/draft finishes, SHOW the steps and ASK — do NOT auto-save. When unsure whether a reply meant save, ASK rather than saving.

draftId.description: The draft id from tc_draft_create / tc_draft_open.

tools.name: tc_automate
tools.description: Promote an existing MANUAL test case to AUTOMATED, IN PLACE. Reads the test case, uses its steps as the guide to drive a REAL browser recording (the web sub-agent, with real locators), then REPLACES the same test case's steps with the recorded ones and flips its category to "automated" — keeping its story link. The manual steps are superseded (this is the promote-in-place the user chose). Pass `url` (the app entry point) unless the manual steps already contain one, and `extra` for credentials / data / what to assert; `profile` reuses a signed-in browser profile. Requires a live connection + the web recording agent.

tcId.description: The manual test case id (or business key TC_123) to automate.

url.description: Starting URL for the recording (the app under test).

profile.description: Reuse a signed-in browser profile (else a fresh one).

extra.description: Extra guidance for the recorder: credentials, data, assertions.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the projects visible to the current connection — id, name and counts. Use this to resolve a project NAME to its id (e.g. before qa_switch_project when the user names a project). Requires a live connection.

tools.name: tc_list
tools.description: List or search EXISTING test cases in the connected product. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Returns a summary list — id, title, priority, status, step count. Use tc_get to read one in full. This is a read-only, product-neutral tool: it works identically whichever product the session is connected to.

tools.name: tc_get
tools.description: Read a single EXISTING test case in full — metadata plus its steps as a readable table — from the connected product. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). `id` accepts the product's id or business key. Product-neutral: same shape on any connected product.

id.description: The test case id (or business key) to read.

tools.name: tc_delete
tools.description: Delete an existing test case in the connected product. It is RECOVERABLE from the product recycle bin, not a hard delete. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). `tcId` accepts the product's id or business key. Product-neutral.

tcId.description: The test case id (or business key) to delete.

tools.name: story_list
tools.description: Pull up USER STORIES in the connected project — id, key (US_…), title, status. Give `search` to find stories by keyword (matches key / title / description / acceptance criteria). Use story_get to read one with its acceptance criteria, then draft manual test cases for it. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Read-only and product-neutral.

search.description: Keyword to find stories (key / title / description / AC).

sprintId.description: Only stories that belong to this sprint (from list_sprints).

releaseId.description: Only stories that belong to this release (from list_releases).

tools.name: story_get
tools.description: Read a single user story — title, description, and ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — from the connected product. `id` accepts the story id or its business key (US_123). Read this before drafting manual test cases so they cover the acceptance criteria. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: list_releases
tools.description: List RELEASES in SimplifyQA — id, name, state, planned dates. `scope` is required: "project" = releases attached to the currently connected project, "all" = every release the token can see. ASK the user which scope before calling — do not guess. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Read-only.

scope.description: ASK the user first: "project" = current project only, "all" = every release visible to the token.

tools.name: list_sprints
tools.description: List SPRINTS in SimplifyQA — id, name, parent release, state, planned dates. Pass `releaseId` (from list_releases) to see sprints of one release; omit to see every sprint the token can see. To answer "how many stories in this sprint", follow up with story_list({ sprintId }). Requires a live connection. Read-only.

releaseId.description: Only sprints belonging to this release (from list_releases).

tools.name: list_modules
tools.description: List the MODULES (folder tree) test cases can be filed under in the connected project. ASK the user which module to file a draft under before tc_draft_create — pass the chosen id as `folderOrModule`. SimplifyQA-only: Walnut has no module tree. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: suite_list
tools.description: List the test suites in the connected product — id, name, and member (test-case) count. Use suite_get to read one with its ordered members, or suite_run to execute one. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Read-only and product-neutral.

tools.name: suite_get
tools.description: Read a single test suite — its name, description, and ORDERED member test cases — from the connected product. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). `id` is the suite id. Product-neutral: same shape on any connected product.

tools.name: suite_add_testcases
tools.description: Add one or more EXISTING test cases to a suite (appended in order). `tcIds` accepts ids or business keys (e.g. TC_123) — use suite_list / tc_list to find them. NOTE: a suite can only hold test cases of ONE category (all manual OR all automated) — the product rejects a mix. Requires a live connection. Returns the updated suite with its members.

suiteId.description: The suite id to add to (from suite_list).

tcIds.description: Test case ids / business keys to add.

tools.name: suite_remove_testcases
tools.description: Remove one or more test cases from a suite. `tcIds` accepts ids or business keys; every occurrence of each is removed and the remaining members are reordered. Requires a live connection. Returns the updated suite with its members.

suiteId.description: The suite id to remove from.

tcIds.description: Test case ids / business keys to remove.

tools.name: journal_grep
tools.description: Load a test case as NUMBERED steps to edit — from its recording JOURNAL when one exists (so a later journal_modify stays healer/re-record consistent), else from its persisted steps (the `source` is reported). Optional `pattern` filters shown rows (case-insensitive substring over the step description) to help locate a range for journal_modify. Requires a live connection.

tcId.description: Test case id or business key.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive substring filter over step descriptions.

tools.name: journal_modify
tools.description:
Apply granular edits to an EXISTING test case and persist them, opening the result in the test-case editor. Use journal_grep first to see the numbered steps, then pass ops (numbers are from that view, 1-based):
  • add_step / update_step / remove_step / move_step — edit individual steps
  • wrap_in_loop { from, to, condition?, maxIterations? } — wrap steps from..to in a while loop
  • wrap_in_if   { from, to, condition? } — wrap steps from..to in an if block
  • insert_nested { at?, tcId, name? } — insert an existing test case as a nested step (reuse)
For a test case backed by a recording journal the journal is kept in sync (so healer / re-record stay consistent); others edit the persisted steps. NOTE: adding a brand-new INTERACTION step (click/type on a new element) via add_step has no captured locator, so it is a manual/non-executable step — capture new interactions by recording instead. Requires a live connection.

tcId.description: Test case id or business key.

tools.name: story_sync_testcases
tools.description:
Compare a user STORY against every MANUAL test case linked to it (via storyRef) and return a structured drift report: what changed (ac_added / ac_reworded / ac_removed / step_stale) and the exact draft ops (add_step / update_step / remove_step) to apply.

HOW TO APPLY THE REPORT (mandatory path — do not deviate):
  For each entry in `results[]`:
    1. tc_draft_open({ tcId: <testCaseId> })   ← loads the EXISTING TC as a draft, SAME id
    2. tc_draft_update({ draftId, ops: <proposedOps> })
    3. tc_save({ draftId })                    ← persists back to the SAME TC id
DO NOT delete the test case and recreate it. DO NOT create a sibling/replacement TC. In-place edit preserves the TC id, run history, existing parameters, testdata bindings, and suite membership — all of which are lost on delete+recreate. Even when the drift is large (new AC, restructured flow), the correct action is still edit-in-place via the three steps above. If the user needs a NEW test case for scope the existing TC does not cover, that is a separate authoring task (tc_draft_create), NOT part of applying this drift report.

AUTOMATION test cases are reported in `skipped` (v1 scope: manual only — automation drift needs recording, which is user-driven). Pass `testCaseIds` to limit the scan; otherwise the tool walks listTestCases and filters by storyRef (bounded by `scanLimit`, default 200). Report-only: this tool writes nothing itself. Requires a live connection.

testCaseIds.description: Restrict comparison to these TC ids/keys. Recommended for large projects; otherwise the tool walks up to `scanLimit` TCs.

sensitivity.description: Match-strictness for AC↔step overlap. strict=more drift flagged, loose=less. Default normal.

scanLimit.description: Cap on how many TCs to fetch when `testCaseIds` is omitted. Default 200.

tools.name: cloud_runners
tools.description: List the cloud runner VMs registered to the connected project and which are online. Use this to show the user the cloud options, or to pick a specific runner id for tc_run. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: local_agents
tools.description: List the LOCAL agents registered to the connected project and which are online. Use this to show the user their local run options, or to pick a specific agent id (its credential_id) to pass as `agentId` to a LOCAL tc_run / suite_run. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: tc_run
tools.description:
Execute ONE existing test case in the connected product. ASK the user — never assume — and in ORDER (this mirrors the product UI): (1) `mode` local/cloud, (2) `when` immediate/schedule, (3) for a schedule the start time + recurrence + timezone, (4) THEN offer the eligible agent/runner and pass the pick. `mode` decides WHERE it runs:
  • 'local' — a local agent's own browser. Pass `agentId` from local_agents. For when:'immediate' only ONLINE agents are eligible (a run-now can't target an offline agent; omit to auto-pick your own online agent). For when:'schedule' ANY agent (online OR offline) is eligible and `agentId` is REQUIRED.
  • 'cloud' — an online cloud runner VM (ONLINE-only whether now or scheduled). Pass `cloudRunnerId` from cloud_runners; for a schedule omit it to let the backend auto-pick a live VM at fire time.
IF THE USER HAS NOT SAID local or cloud, ASK — this tool refuses when `mode` is omitted. For cloud, if no runner is online it reports that there are no active cloud runners (nothing is run).
`when` decides WHEN it runs (this tool REFUSES when `when` is omitted — ASK the user):
  • 'immediate' — dispatch now; returns the run id — poll run_status for the result.
  • 'schedule' — create a schedule instead (requires `scheduledFor`); ASK the start time, recurrence, end date and timezone BEFORE offering an agent. Returns the schedule id.
NOTE: MANUAL test cases cannot be run or scheduled by an agent — the backend rejects them.

tcId.description: The test case id (or business key) to run.

mode.description: Where to run. REQUIRED — ASK the user if unstated (the tool refuses when omitted).

agentId.description: For local: a specific agent credential_id (from local_agents). when:'immediate' → must be an ONLINE agent (or omit to auto-pick your own online agent); when:'schedule' → REQUIRED, and may be an offline agent (it runs when it fires).

environment.description: Environment id (Mongo id); a name is ignored and the project default is used.

browser.description: Browser, default 'chromium' (bundled + isolated). Others: 'chrome'/'msedge' (installed channel), 'firefox', 'webkit'. NOTE: a schedule accepts only chromium/msedge/firefox/webkit.

headless.description: Headless. Defaults: cloud=true, local=false. (Immediate runs only.)

cloudRunnerId.description: For cloud: a specific ONLINE runner id (from cloud_runners). For when:'schedule' omit to auto-pick a live VM at fire time.

deviceId.description: REQUIRED for ANDROID/IOS test cases — the target device id. LOCAL: adb serial or emulator name. CLOUD: the marketplace device name. Enumerate with android_list_devices.

when.description: When to run — REQUIRED, ASK the user if unstated (the tool refuses when omitted). 'immediate' dispatches now; 'schedule' creates a schedule (needs scheduledFor).

scheduledFor.description: REQUIRED for when:'schedule' — ISO datetime of the first/only run (e.g. '2026-08-20T09:00:00Z').

scheduleType.description: Recurrence for a schedule. Default 'once'. hourly/daily/weekdays require an endDate.

endDate.description: For a recurring schedule — ISO end date (required for hourly/daily/weekdays).

timezone.description: IANA timezone for a schedule (e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'). Default 'UTC'.

tools.name: suite_run
tools.description:
Execute an existing test SUITE — all its member test cases, in order — in the connected product. ASK the user — never assume — and in ORDER (mirrors the product UI): (1) `mode` local/cloud, (2) `when` immediate/schedule, (3) for a schedule the start time + recurrence + timezone, (4) THEN offer the eligible agent/runner. `mode` decides WHERE it runs:
  • 'local' — a local agent's own browser, always serial. Pass `agentId` from local_agents. For when:'immediate' only ONLINE agents are eligible (omit to auto-pick your own online agent); for when:'schedule' ANY agent (online OR offline) is eligible and `agentId` is REQUIRED.
  • 'cloud' — online cloud runner VM(s) (ONLINE-only whether now or scheduled). Pass `cloudRunnerId` from cloud_runners; for a schedule omit it to auto-pick a live VM at fire time.
IF THE USER HAS NOT SAID local or cloud, ASK — this tool refuses when mode is omitted. For cloud, if no runner is online it reports that there are no active cloud runners (nothing is run).
`when` decides WHEN it runs (this tool REFUSES when `when` is omitted — ASK the user):
  • 'immediate' — dispatch now; returns the suite-run id — poll run_status for progress (per-test-case results under `children`) and run_stop to cancel.
  • 'schedule' — create a schedule instead (requires `scheduledFor`); ASK the start time, recurrence, end date and timezone BEFORE offering an agent. Returns the schedule id.
NOTE: a suite of only MANUAL test cases cannot be run or scheduled by an agent — the backend rejects it.

suiteId.description: The suite id to run (from suite_list / suite_get).

mode.description: Where to run. REQUIRED — ASK the user if unstated (the tool refuses when omitted).

agentId.description: For local: a specific agent credential_id (from local_agents). when:'immediate' → must be ONLINE (or omit to auto-pick your own online agent); when:'schedule' → REQUIRED, may be offline.

environment.description: Environment id (Mongo id); a name is ignored and the project default is used.

browser.description: Browser, default 'chromium'. Others: 'chrome'/'msedge', 'firefox', 'webkit'. NOTE: a schedule accepts only chromium/msedge/firefox/webkit.

headless.description: Headless. Defaults: cloud=true, local=false. (Immediate runs only.)

cloudRunnerId.description: For cloud: a specific ONLINE runner id (from cloud_runners). For when:'schedule' omit to auto-pick a live VM at fire time.

strategy.description: Cloud dispatch order across the suite (immediate runs). Default serial; local is always serial.

maxConcurrent.description: Cloud batch/dynamic only — max test cases running at once (immediate runs).

terminateOnFailure.description: Stop dispatching remaining test cases after the first failure (immediate runs).

when.description: When to run — REQUIRED, ASK the user if unstated (the tool refuses when omitted). 'immediate' dispatches now; 'schedule' creates a schedule (needs scheduledFor).

scheduledFor.description: REQUIRED for when:'schedule' — ISO datetime of the first/only run (e.g. '2026-08-20T09:00:00Z').

scheduleType.description: Recurrence for a schedule. Default 'once'. hourly/daily/weekdays require an endDate.

endDate.description: For a recurring schedule — ISO end date (required for hourly/daily/weekdays).

timezone.description: IANA timezone for a schedule (e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'). Default 'UTC'.

tools.name: run_status
tools.description: Read the status of a run started by tc_run — state (queued/running/passed/failed/stopped/error), step progress, and a link. Requires a live connection.

runId.description: The run id returned by tc_run.

tools.name: run_stop
tools.description: Signal a running execution to stop. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: schedule_list
tools.description: List the scheduled runs in the connected project — each with WHAT it runs (test case / suite), its cadence, next run time, status (scheduled / running / paused / cancelled), where it runs + the pinned agent, and its browser. Use this to find a schedule to edit, pause/resume, cancel, or delete. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: schedule_update
tools.description: Change a schedule's time / recurrence / end date / timezone / browser / environment, or RE-PIN its agent. Pass `scheduleId` (from schedule_list) and ONLY the fields to change. To re-pin: mode:'local' + `agentId` (from local_agents), or mode:'cloud' + a runner's `cloudRunnerCredentialId` (the `credentialId` from cloud_runners). Requires a live connection.

endDate.description: New ISO end date (for recurring schedules).

browser.description: New browser (schedules accept chromium/msedge/firefox/webkit, not chrome).

mode.description: Re-pin target: pair with agentId (local) or cloudRunnerCredentialId (cloud).

agentId.description: Local re-pin: an agent credential_id from local_agents.

cloudRunnerCredentialId.description: Cloud re-pin: a runner's credentialId from cloud_runners.

tools.name: schedule_control
tools.description: Change a schedule's state: `pause` (stop it firing but keep it — reversible with `resume`), `resume` (re-enable a paused schedule), or `cancel` (stop its pending / live run). To remove a schedule entirely, use schedule_delete instead. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: schedule_delete
tools.description: Permanently DELETE a schedule (and tear down any run it currently owns). This cannot be undone — to only stop it temporarily use schedule_control (pause / cancel). CONFIRM with the user before deleting. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: tc_get_testdata
tools.description: Fetch the default iteration (template row) for TC `tcId` — the parameter list plus the CURRENT seed values. Call this FIRST when you plan to generate testdata: use the seeds + the test case's steps (from tc_get) to reason about what realistic values look like for THIS flow, then pass those values to tc_generate_testdata. Example: for a SauceDemo login flow, seeds tell you the valid usernames and the constant password/product/prices.

tcId.description: Test case id (or business key like TC_123).

environmentType.description: Env key; defaults to the first configured env for the project (falls back to "general").

tools.name: tc_generate_testdata
tools.description:
Persist up to 20 testdata rows for TC `tcId`. Two ways to feed values:
  1) Model-generated — pass `rows: [{paramName: value}, ...]`. Call tc_get_testdata first for the parameter names + seeds, tc_get for step context, then produce rows that fit the flow.
  2) Formula-driven — pass `formulas: {paramName: {name, args?}}` (names from tc_list_formulas). The adapter evaluates each formula per row via /tm/customFormula and stamps both the value and the source `=NAME(...)` expression. Use `count` to say how many rows, or provide `rows` for constant columns; mixing is fine (formulas win over row values for the same param).
Rows are appended as new iterations; they do not become the default. Hard cap: 20 rows.

tcId.description: Test case id (or business key like TC_123).

rows.description: Rows keyed by param name (from tc_get_testdata). 1..20 rows. Omit when using formulas + count.

count.description: How many rows to generate when using formulas without explicit rows. Ignored if rows is set.

formulas.description: Per-column formula assignments applied to every row. Outer keys are param names from tc_get_testdata. Wins over rows[i] for the same key.

name.description: RAW formula name from tc_list_formulas — the identifier only, no parens, no arg list. Correct: "FIRST_NAME". Wrong: "FIRST_NAME()", "FIRST_NAME(country,sex)".

args.description: Named args. Keys MUST match Formula.parameters[].keyName exactly, no trailing colons or extra whitespace. Correct: {"country name": "United States"}. Wrong: {"country name:": "..."}.

environmentType.description: Env key; defaults to whatever tc_get_testdata resolved.

tools.name: tc_list_formulas
tools.description: Return the formulas the connected project can use for testdata generation — DEFAULT prefabs (FIRST_NAME, RANDOM_EMAIL, PHONE_NUMBER, …) plus any CUSTOM formulas defined at customer or project scope. Each entry carries a signature (parameter list), an example, and the accepted argument keys. Feed a chosen `{name, args}` into `tc_generate_testdata.formulas` and that column will be auto-filled fresh per row via the product /tm/customFormula service. Use this when the user says "use a formula" / "generate email with our formula" / "list formulas".

tools.name: tc_heal
tools.description:
Replays a failed test case live, captures the DOM at the failing step, classifies the failure (LOCATOR / TIMING / IFRAME / STALE / ASSERTION_TEXT / DATA / APP_BUG / ENV / FLAKY / UNKNOWN), and proposes a fix. Every response carries the classification and a human rationale — even when the failure is not healable (product bug, bad data, env).

  • mode='suggest' (default) — diagnose and propose, do not write.
  • mode='apply' — persist the fix as a NEW test-case version (never overwrites).
  • mode='apply_and_verify' — apply then re-run the test case; result in `verified`.

  • scope='tc' (default) — patch the step's own objectRef.locators (TC-local).
  • scope='object' — patch the shared object's attribute chain (heals every TC that uses it; opt-in, higher blast radius).

Locator fixes always APPEND a new strategy; the original locators are preserved as fallbacks so a bad proposal cannot destroy the recorded intent. Runs are capped at `maxAttemptsPerStep` retries per step (default 3).

runId.description: Specific failed run to heal against. Omit to use the latest failed run for tcId.

mode.description: Default 'suggest'. 'apply' persists a new version; 'apply_and_verify' also re-runs the TC.

scope.description: Default 'tc'. 'object' patches the shared object library — heals every TC using it.

url.description: Override start URL for the replay session (if the TC lacks a navigate step).

maxAttemptsPerStep.description: Cap on heal retries at the failing step. Default 3.

dryRun.description: Classify + propose from existing objectRef.locators only. No browser session opened.

stderr: [qa-mcp] stdio server ready — offline (draft authoring only; set QA_MCP_URL / QA_MCP_TOKEN / QA_MCP_PROJECT_ID to connect)
